channel.title: AeroSpork
channel.description: Updates for AeroSpork, an i3-like tiling window manager for macOS.

item.description:
Settings, redesigned

Every pane got a full pass — same seven panes, now behaving like a native macOS preferences window.

  • Native pane toolbar. The settings window uses the standard macOS preferences toolbar, remembers which pane you were on, and titles the window after it.
  • Raw TOML is now a real editor. Line numbers, native Find (⌘F), horizontal scrolling instead of wrapping, restrained TOML highlighting, a section jump menu, cursor line/column readout, and parser errors that link to the failing line.
  • Keys. Bindings grouped by what they do, search across every mode at once, one-click Duplicate, and a mode picker that stays usable however many modes you define.
  • Monitors. The arrangement schematic is now the control: click a monitor to see its details and the workspaces pinned to it, then pin, move, or unpin workspaces from a menu right there. Assignments too rich for the editor are shown as such and preserved untouched — editing one workspace can no longer re-spell another's regex or fallback list.
  • The settings window is finally resizable. It was silently fixed at its ideal size; the documented 780×520 minimum is now real.
  • Window Rules. Guided controls for the common cases — float/tile and send-to-workspace — with your exact command preserved verbatim whenever it says something the controls can't.
  • Gaps. A live preview, and "same value" links so symmetric gaps take one edit instead of four.
  • Events. Real command placeholders, per-event explanations, and a heads-up when callbacks inherit your shell environment.

Also in this release

  • The standard "About AeroSpork" menu item is back.
  • Short-value fields (workspace names, the assignment picker) are sized to their content instead of stretching across the row.
  • Badge text contrast now meets WCAG AA in light mode, and the monitor schematic stays legible with asymmetric arrangements (an ultrawide above two 4Ks no longer overlaps its labels).
  • "Choose app…" in Window Rules now opens as a sheet on the settings window. It used to open behind everything — a menu-bar app can't bring a detached panel forward — which read as the button hanging the app.
  • Backup timestamps are now locale-independent; if your system uses a non-Gregorian calendar, backups made by older versions may show raw filenames in the Restore menu once.

Fixes the settings window slowly growing your config file.

Saving from Settings no longer adds blank lines

Every save through the settings window added a blank line before the section it rewrote, and dropped the newline at the end of the file. One save was invisible. But settings apply on a short delay, so a minute of adjusting things is several saves — and the file grew a line each time, leaving a widening gap in the middle and \ No newline at end of file at the bottom of every diff.

If your config lives in a dotfiles repository, this is the change that stops it showing up as noise there.

Nothing you wrote is touched. Blank lines you put in yourself stay exactly as they are — the fix only suppresses the ones the editor was adding.

Universal (arm64 + x86_64), signed with a Developer ID, notarized and stapled.

Install

brew install --cask wbsmolen/tap/aerospork

Or download aerospork-v1.1.7.zip, move aerospork-v1.1.7/AeroSpork.app to /Applications, and grant Accessibility permission when prompted. Optionally put aerospork-v1.1.7/bin/aerospork on your PATH for the CLI.

AeroSpork-1.1.7.zip is the Sparkle update archive — the same app without the CLI, man pages or licence files. It exists for the updater; prefer the versioned zip for a manual install.

Fixes workspace memory doing nothing after a reboot, a case where editing a window rule could damage unrelated parts of your config, and the missing licence in every previous download.

Workspace memory now works on a cold boot

1.1.5 remembered which workspace each window was on, but at login it forgot any application that had not finished starting. AeroSpork launches alongside every other login item and macOS's own window restore, so a slow app was absent from the first snapshot — and that snapshot was written straight over the memory, deleting its entry before the app ever appeared.

So the case the feature exists for, restarting your Mac, was the one it skipped. It now waits for those windows instead of forgetting them.

Also fixed: if a logout was cancelled by another app, AeroSpork kept running with its memory frozen and never saved again for the rest of the session.

Editing a window rule could damage unrelated config

Three ways, all fixed:

  • A regex containing [ — an ordinary thing to write in a window-title matcher — silently

switched off every safety check for the rest of the file. Those checks are what stop the editor rewriting things it cannot represent, including a monitor pinned by hardware fingerprint, so an edit elsewhere could quietly degrade it to a plain name.

  • A comment after a section header, like [on-window] # my rules, made that section

unrecognisable to the writer. It added a second copy instead of replacing it, so every rule in the table applied twice.

  • A monitor written as a list of fallbacks was reduced to its first entry — including on rows you

did not touch, since one edit rewrites the whole section. It is now refused with a pointer to the Raw TOML tab rather than silently truncated.

The licence was missing from every download

legal/LICENSE.txt was a link to a file that was never included in the archive, so every release shipped the four third-party licences and not AeroSpork's own. The release now carries it, and the packaging refuses to build an archive with a broken link in it.

Update notes and the state file

The Check for Updates dialog showed a blank "what's new" pane. It now shows these notes.

Workspace memory moved from /tmp to ~/Library/Caches/com.wbs.aerospork/workspace-memory.json and is readable only by you. It lists which applications are running and which monitors are attached, which no other account on the machine needs to see, and /tmp is writable by anyone — a file planted there decided where your windows went. Upgrading leaves the old file behind; it is ignored and safe to delete.

Universal (arm64 + x86_64), signed with a Developer ID, notarized and stapled.

Install

brew install --cask wbsmolen/tap/aerospork

Or download aerospork-v1.1.6.zip, move aerospork-v1.1.6/AeroSpork.app to /Applications, and grant Accessibility permission when prompted. Optionally put aerospork-v1.1.6/bin/aerospork on your PATH for the CLI.

AeroSpork-1.1.6.zip is the Sparkle update archive — the same app without the CLI, man pages or licence files. It exists for the updater; prefer the versioned zip for a manual install.
